title: Opt-in split and A:X+Y far-pointer conventions crash when a far pointer is followed by another argument
summary: Under the opt-in +mos-farcc-split or +mos-farcc-axy far-pointer calling convention, a function whose far-pointer argument (assigned by the custom CC_MOS_FarPtrSplit / CC_MOS_FarPtrAXY assigner) is followed by any other argument aborts in CallLowering::handleAssignments during the IRTranslator: two far pointers, or one far pointer then an i8. The release build aborts with no diagnostic (exit 134). The matching call site does not terminate: IRTranslator memory grows until an address-space limit gives "LLVM ERROR: out of memory", or the kernel OOM killer ends llc. A single far-pointer argument compiles, which is all the existing farcc_split/farcc_axy gates exercise. The same holds with +mos-xy16 and on the B1-B4 candidate. The default Imag32 convention and the opt-in Stack convention are not affected. Found while testing the B1 stack fallback against these conventions (plan docs/plans/2026-09-30-far-prerequisite-defects.md, Outcome).
attribution: Reproduction, prior-work audit and this record: Claude Code 2.1.283 t3-opus-med subagent, model Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), medium reasoning effort (t3-opus-med agent definition); dispatched from session f79adc39-72b4-4dc5-abc1-849c14c5ce96.
unknowns: Root cause not investigated: the release build aborts without a message and no assertions build carries the far-pointer conventions. The custom VA handling in handleAssignments (j += NumArgRegs - 1) or MOSCallLowering assignCustomValue is the likely site.
Whether these conventions ever handled a second argument is unknown; their gates only pass a single far pointer.
The i8-then-far order compiles under split but aborts under axy (A is taken, so the far pointer is not custom-assigned); that case overlaps register exhaustion and is not separately characterised.

prior_work.source_assessment: CC_MOS_FarPtrSplit and CC_MOS_FarPtrAXY push two or three custom CCValAssigns per far pointer, and MOSCallLowering assignCustomValue (incoming and outgoing) composes them. Nothing in the source, the variant plans or the gates covers a far pointer followed by another argument.
prior_work.binary_assessment: The downstream release llc 9031686c aborts (134) on two-far.ll and far-then-i8.ll in split and axy, with and without +mos-xy16, and compiles single-far.ll. The B1-B4 candidate llc behaves identically. caller.ll exhausts memory on both.
prior_work.decision: mos-far-pointer-arg-exhaustion covers the default Imag32 convention running out of RL quads and is fixed; it lists this crash only as an unknown. This failure needs no exhaustion (one far pointer plus an i8) and lies in custom-value call lowering, so it is a distinct defect. No existing record, TODO item or patch covers it. New canonical record.
